pack.title: Condescending strangers
pack.description: Unsolicited superiority from people you'll never see again. Brief and gone.

scenarios.setting: Bookstore. You ask where the new releases are; the clerk sighs audibly.
scenarios.jab: It's literally signed everywhere. Just look around.

replies.line: And yet here I am, asking you. Point, please.
replies.why: It calmly re-asks the question, which makes the sigh the awkward part.
Two words that skip the attitude and collect the answer.

replies.line: Long day? Point me there and I'll get out of your hair.
replies.why: Naming their day with sympathy buys you the help and their humanity.

replies.line: The signs cover books, not manners. Where to?
replies.why: It answers rudeness in kind, which wins the moment and loses the high ground.
A fake diagnosis makes them the good Samaritan instead of the scold.

trap.line: Let me speak to your manager about your attitude.
trap.why: Escalating over a sigh spends ten minutes to feel worse about a bookstore.

scenarios.setting: Gym. You rerack your weights; a stranger watches, arms crossed.
scenarios.jab: You know that's not how you do that exercise, right?

replies.line: My trainer and I will take it under advisement.
replies.why: Citing your own expert ends his coaching career in one sentence.
It declines the lesson before it's offered, with thanks as the full stop.

replies.line: Appreciate it — I'm following a program though.
replies.why: Thanks plus a plan respects the intent while declining the content.

replies.line: Shh — I'm doing the wrong version on purpose. Chaos reps.
replies.why: Absurd commitment to the bit makes correcting you feel ridiculous.
It frames the correction as art criticism, which no one continues.
